evidence: The films were highly crystalline unlike other ALD grown films reported 15 and did not require post-annealing. Fig. 1a shows a long duration θ-2θ scan of MoS₂ grown at 300 °C for 2000 cycles revealing the reflections corresponding to MoS₂ and c-sapphire. The Raman spectra show strong signals due to the in-plane E12g and the out-of-plane A1g optical phonon modes. The electronic structure and optical band gap of MoS₂ are dependent on the number of layers or the film thickness. We investigated the optical properties of MoS₂ thin films by Raman scattering excited by 514 nm laser under ambient conditions (Fig. 1b). The surface morphology and thickness of the MoS₂ epitaxial films were examined by FE-SEM. The atomic force microscope (AFM) topographic image in Fig. 2i shows a 2D view of the surface of a 2000 cycle sample on c-sapphire. The HRTEM image of MoS₂ and sapphire interface and the FFT pattern from individual layers are given in Fig. 3 (b) and (c). The FESEM images in Fig. 4 show the growth of MoS₂ nanowall network on the stainless steel substrate which we have used in the battery application. The as-deposited MoS₂ was characterized by FESEM, EDAX and Raman spectroscopy.
